title: Fear Index Hits 37. What Happens Next?
description:
Wall Street's fear index, the Cboe Volatility Index (VIX), closed at 37.37 on Nov 20, 2026, up from 15.01 on Oct 6, the day the S&P 500 set its record. The S&P 500 fell 7 days in a row to 6,910.39, 11.6% below that record. We explain what the VIX measures, how rare readings like this are (30+ on about 8% of days since 1990), and what the S&P 500 did after each of the 22 times since 1990 that the VIX first closed above 30: higher a month later 15 of 22 times, higher a year later 14 of 21 times (median +15%), with 2008 as the big exception.

Sources: Yahoo Finance daily closes for the Cboe Volatility Index (^VIX, from 1990), the S&P 500 (^GSPC) and the Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC), saved Nov 20, 2026 after the close. FRED (Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis): DGS10 (10-year Treasury yield), CPIAUCSL (CPI). Spike and return statistics are our calculations, prices only (no dividends). A 'first spike' is the first close at 30 or higher after at least 60 trading days below 30.
